title: Decibels and the S meter
idea: Decibels count power ratios. 3 dB doubles, 10 dB is ten times, and one S unit is 6 dB, about four times the power.

compare.how: S1 to S9, each step about 6 dB. Used up to S9.
Above S9 the meter is marked in dB: S9 +10, +20, +40.

traps.why: 20 dB is not 20 times. Every 10 dB multiplies by 10: 10 x 10 = 100 times.
2 times is only 3 dB. One S unit is 6 dB: 2 x 2 = 4 times.
6 dB is four times the power. Twice is 3 dB.
12 dB is two S units. One S unit is 6 dB.
1 dB down leaves 0.794 of the power, so 1 - 0.794 = 20.6 percent is lost.
An S meter reads the strength of signals you receive.
